# Open-Set Recognition

A classifier trained on `K` categories must, by construction, map **every** input onto one of them.
Open-set recognition (OSR) removes that assumption: the model may name a known class **or reject
the input as unknown**, and both are correct answers.

The failure it fixes is not inaccuracy but *silence*. Train on cats, dogs and horses, show it a
frog, and the network returns whichever known class looks most similar — usually with high
confidence. A softmax layer makes this unavoidable: its outputs sum to 1 across the known classes,
so there is nowhere for probability mass to go except onto a wrong label.

| Ability | Closed-set | Open-set |
|---|:--:|:--:|
| Classify a known class | ✓ | ✓ |
| Recognise "this is none of the known classes" | ✗ | ✓ |
| Cope with a changing, open world | ✗ | ✓ |

## Why it matters, per the study

Three arguments, in the order [[research-methodologies-open-set-recognition]] makes them:
**safety** (a face-recognition system that must choose will match a stranger to a friend; a
perception stack will read a stroller as a motorcycle), **annotation cost** (supervised learning
needs every class labelled by hand and can never be exhaustive), and **fit to deployment** (the
real world is open-ended by nature).

## The three families

| Family | Method | Core idea |
|---|---|---|
| **Traditional** | confidence / distance threshold | reject anything scoring below a chosen cut; simple and effective, the hard part is picking the threshold |
| | distance-based rejection | reject samples far from every known-class prototype in feature space |
| **Statistical** | Extreme Value Theory | model the *tail* of the score distribution, where outliers live |
| | **OpenMax** | replace softmax with a layer that hands probability mass to an explicit unknown class — [[openmax-and-extreme-value-theory]] |
| **Deep** | metric learning | compact, well-separated features leave empty space for unknowns to fall into |
| | generative | synthesise unknown-looking samples, or use reconstruction error as the signal — [[generative-adversarial-network]] |
| | self-supervised / contrastive / Bayesian / evidential / ViT | stronger representations, uncertainty estimated directly |

## The result that unifies them

> "A recurring modern finding ties the families together: **a good closed-set classifier is"
> — Research Methodologies/README.md, 2026-07-11

— already a good open-set detector (Vaze et al., ICLR 2022). Improving plain accuracy tends to
improve the confidence and feature scores that OSR relies on, which makes the two goals far more
aligned than the taxonomy suggests. It also sets an uncomfortable bar for any dedicated method: it
must beat a merely better-trained baseline.

## Where the study takes it

The generative branch is developed in full and ends on OpenGAN (Kong & Ramanan, ICCV 2021), which
moves the discrimination into **feature space** and selects the model checkpoint on a small
held-out open set. Benchmarks are cited, not reproduced —
[[report-cites-benchmarks-rather-than-reproducing]].

`confidence: high` — the content is read directly from three source documents that agree with each
other, and it is textbook material corroborated by nine cited papers.
